options.text: Each outside number must equal the sum of its own row or column using the distinct entries $1$ through $9$.
Any nine integers may fill the cells, even with repeats, if the printed outside sums look large.
The $3$ by $3$ grid shape comes from first choosing the numbers $1$ through $9$.
Only the printed word grid decides the fill, without using the outside sums.

teacher.key_rationale: Distinct 1–9 fill the cells and each outside total must match its row or column sum. Allowing repeats omits the fill rule. Saying 1–9 create the grid shape reverses the relation. Chasing the printed word grid is surface capture.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source figure as a 3-by-3 grid with some filled cells and outside row/column sum labels.

stem:
Nandini studies the diagram of a $3$ by $3$ grid. Each cell must hold a different number from $1$ through $9$. The outside numbers are the sums of their rows or columns.

Which claim correctly states how the grid may be filled or rejected?
